name: dsprites
description: dsprites is a synthetic image dataset of 2D shapes with controlled factors of variation (shape, scale, rotation, x/y position) used to evaluate unsupervised representation learning and disentanglement methods. It measures how well models learn independent latent factors without supervision and is commonly used to compare disentanglement metrics and algorithms. The dataset is intentionally simple and synthetic, making it useful for controlled experiments but less representative of real-world imagery.
reputation: Widely used in disentanglement and representation learning research but criticized for being overly synthetic and not reflecting real-world complexity.
